name: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver module (red board)
description: Drives 2 DC motors or 1 bipolar stepper up to 2 A per channel. Old and inefficient (about 2 V lost) but robust and cheap.
notes: Voltage drop: the bipolar L298 loses about 1.8-3 V across the bridge at 1 A, so a 6 V motor on a 6 V supply only sees about 4 V. Prefer TB6612FNG for 5-12 V motors under 1.2 A.
5V-EN jumper: ON = the onboard 78M05 makes 5 V from +12V (needs at least about 7 V in, keep the input at or below 12 V). OFF = +5V is an input you must supply.
Logic inputs are TTL: HIGH above 2.3 V, so 3.3 V microcontrollers drive it fine. Input absolute max 7 V.
The module has 8 flyback diodes and a heatsink. Above about 1 A per channel the heatsink gets very hot.
Terminal side order and labels vary between clones (some print 12V as VMS or VCC). Check the silkscreen.
Connect the module GND to the microcontroller GND.

pins.name: +12V
pins.label: 12V
pins.note: Motor supply (also feeds the 5 V regulator while the 5V-EN jumper is on). Keep at or below 12 V with the jumper on; remove the jumper for 12-35 V and feed +5V from your controller.

pins.name: +5V
pins.label: 5V
pins.note: With the 5V-EN jumper ON: 5 V output from the onboard 78M05 (about 0.4 A spare). With the jumper OFF: you must feed 5 V logic power IN here.

pins.name: ENA
pins.label: ENA
pins.note: Enable / speed (PWM) for OUT1-OUT2. Jumpered to 5 V by default (full speed); remove the jumper to control speed.

pins.name: ENB
pins.label: ENB
pins.note: Enable / speed for OUT3-OUT4. Jumpered to 5 V by default.

geometry.note: Typical module 43 x 43 x 27 mm with 3 mm holes; positions vary.
